question: What processor core architecture does the PIC32MX family use?
reference_answer: The PIC32MX family uses the 32-bit MIPS32 M4K CPU core with a 5-stage pipeline.

question: What is the operating voltage range for the PIC32MX microcontrollers?
reference_answer: The operating voltage range is 2.3V to 3.6V.

question: What email address is provided for submitting documentation errors and feedback?
reference_answer: Documentation errors and feedback can be submitted via email to docerrors@microchip.com.

question: What is the nominal output frequency of the Fast Internal Oscillator (FRC)?
reference_answer: The Fast Internal Oscillator (FRC) has a nominal output frequency of 8 MHz.

question: What is the fixed output frequency of the Internal Low-Power RC oscillator (LPRC)?
reference_answer: The Internal Low-Power RC oscillator (LPRC) has a fixed output frequency of 31 kHz.

question: What conversion rate is supported by the 10-Bit Analog-to-Digital Converter?
reference_answer: The 10-Bit Analog-to-Digital Converter supports a conversion rate of 500 ksps.

question: What high-current capability is supported on all I/O pins of the microcontroller?
reference_answer: All I/O pins support High-Current Sink/Source capability of 18 mA/18 mA.

question: Which Microchip device model is specifically cited as pin-compatible with the PIC32MX Family?
reference_answer: The PIC32MX Family is pin-compatible with Microchip PIC24FJ128GA010 devices.

question: How many instruction and data hardware break points are available?
reference_answer: There are 6 instruction hardware break points and 2 data hardware break points.

question: By how much can MIPS16e Mode reduce code size?
reference_answer: MIPS16e Mode allows for up to 40% smaller code size.

question: What configuration bit must application code clear to use multiplexed PORTA pins (RA0, RA1, RA4, RA5) for general-purpose I/O on 100-pin devices?
reference_answer: The application code must clear the JTAGEN bit (DDPCON<3> = 0) to use these pins for general-purpose I/O.

question: What are the program memory and data memory sizes for the PIC32MX320F032H model?
reference_answer: The PIC32MX320F032H model features 32 KB of program memory and 8 KB of data memory.

question: What topic is covered in Section 20.0 of the PIC32MX datasheet?
reference_answer: Section 20.0 covers the Parallel Master Port.

question: What standard is the JTAG Boundary Scan compatible with?
reference_answer: The JTAG Boundary Scan is compatible with IEEE Std 1149.2.

question: What is the size of the Boot Flash Memory provided in addition to main program memory?
reference_answer: An additional 12 KB of Boot Flash Memory is provided.

question: What two programming and debugging interfaces are provided on the PIC32MX family?
reference_answer: The two interfaces are a 2-wire interface with unintrusive access and real-time data exchange, and a 4-wire MIPS standard enhanced JTAG interface.

question: What external crystal frequency is the Secondary Oscillator (SOSC) designed to operate with?
reference_answer: The Secondary Oscillator (SOSC) is designed to operate with an external 32.768 kHz crystal.

question: What is the maximum operating frequency range specified for PIC32MX360F512L in Table 1-1?
reference_answer: The operating frequency range is DC to 80 MHz.

question: Which ISO certification does Microchip hold for the quality system of designing and manufacturing development systems?
reference_answer: Microchip holds ISO 9001:2000 certification for the design and manufacture of development systems.

question: How can a user identify the version number of a Microchip data sheet?
reference_answer: The version number is determined by examining the last character of the literature number found on the bottom outside corner of any page.

question: How many 16-bit timers are integrated into the PIC32MX family, and how can they be combined to form 32-bit timers?
reference_answer: The PIC32MX family includes five 16-bit timers/counters, where two 16-bit pairs can combine to form two 32-bit timers.

question: How does the Fail-Safe Clock Monitor handle a main clock failure during system operation?
reference_answer: The Fail-Safe Clock Monitor constantly checks the main clock against a reference signal from the internal oscillator. If the main clock fails, it enables the system to switch to the internal oscillator to maintain low-speed operation or execute a safe shutdown.

question: How does implementing the Real-Time Clock/Calendar (RTCC) module in hardware benefit MCU resources?
reference_answer: By implementing the clock, calendar, and alarm functions directly in hardware, the RTCC module frees up timer resources and program memory space for the core application.

question: Which facility locations earned Microchip ISO/TS-16949:2002 certification for MCU/DSC manufacturing and design?
reference_answer: Microchip received ISO/TS-16949:2002 certification for its headquarters, design, and wafer fabrication facilities in Chandler and Tempe, Arizona; Gresham, Oregon; and design centers in California and India.

question: What execution performance benchmark in DMIPS/MHz does the CPU core achieve, and what hardware acceleration unit supports 32-bit integer math?
reference_answer: The MIPS32 M4K CPU core achieves up to 1.5 DMIPS/MHz and features a single-cycle multiply and high-performance divide unit for 32-bit integer math execution.

question: How many UART modules does the PIC32MX family contain, and what built-in hardware encoding standard do they support for serial communications?
reference_answer: The PIC32MX family contains two independent UART modules that feature built-in hardware encoders and decoders supporting IrDA communications.

question: Does the PIC32MX microcontroller feature an integrated Ethernet MAC controller?
reference_answer: No, an integrated Ethernet MAC controller is not supported or listed among the peripheral features of the PIC32MX family.

question: Does the PIC32MX family support Wi-Fi wireless networking on-chip?
reference_answer: No, the document does not list Wi-Fi wireless networking as a feature supported by the PIC32MX family.

question: Is the CPU architecture of the PIC32MX family 64-bit?
reference_answer: No, the CPU core is a 32-bit RISC architecture (MIPS32 M4K) and is not 64-bit.

question: How many hardware breakpoints are available on the PIC32MX3XXFXXX General Purpose family?
reference_answer: There are 6 instruction breakpoints and 2 data breakpoints[cite: 3].

question: What is the operating frequency for the PIC32MX4XXFXXX USB Family devices?

question: Is PORTA present on 64-pin devices?
reference_answer: No, PORTA is not present on 64-pin devices[cite: 3].

question: What is the function of the AVDD pin?
reference_answer: It is the Positive Supply for Analog Modules[cite: 3].

question: What is the function of the MCLR pin and how is a Reset triggered using it?
reference_answer: The MCLR pin is the Master Clear (Device Reset) Input, and bringing this line low causes a Reset[cite: 3].
